description: module value entries: the selected entry's static reference closure evaluates at invocation start, dependency-ordered; entries outside the closure do not evaluate
comment: The case body is the selected entry and the functions map holds the module's entries. An entry whose literal value is a function body is callable by name; any other entry is a value entry.

cases.description: value entries in the entry's closure evaluate before the entry function runs
a value entry outside the entry's closure does not evaluate
cases.comment: Unlike a $let binding, an unreferenced module entry never runs: entry evaluation is scoped to the selected entry's static reference closure, so the failing entry is inert for this invocation.

cases.description: a referenced value entry evaluates at invocation start even when no runtime branch reads it
cases.comment: The closure is static: the reference from the untaken branch is enough, so the entry's failure fails the invocation.

cases.description: the reference closure continues through a called module function
cases.comment: The call-position exemption removes only the edge to the function itself; the value entries its body references in value position join the closure, so the failing entry evaluates even though the selected entry never references it directly.

cases.description: a dependency cycle among evaluated value entries is a cycle error
cases.error: Circular variable dependency detected: A -> B -> A

cases.description: a module value entry referenced from a closure body is captured by value
cases.comment: Module functions and builtins resolve by name and are never captured; module value entries are the other half of the same rule — the closure's record carries the evaluated value, so a resumed continuation never re-enters module entries.
